clue.text: An unlikely prospect has great desire to get really good

parts.note: someone who longs for something has a great desire for it
hot is slang for excellent or really good, as in 'not so hot'

explanation.surface: A no-hoper who badly wants to improve.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet or contender with little chance of winning is an outsider, an improbable candidate.

clue.text: Foreign characters love silly games

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of games are jumbled into nonsense order

explanation.surface: Someone from abroad who adores playing daft games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' makes MEGAS. 'Foreign characters' suggests strangers, but means letters of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters of the Greek alphabet are characters from a foreign script.

clue.text: Sort of policeman to overthrow an obstacle to process

indicators.note: overthrowing turns things upside down, so in this down clue the phrase is read from the bottom up

parts.note: an gives the article A
a drag is something that holds back progress

explanation.surface: An officer is called on to bring down a barrier blocking proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overthrow' turns A DRAG upside down. The Garda is the police force of the Republic of Ireland, and a member of it is also called a garda.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish police officer is called a garda, after the Garda Siochana force.

clue.text: Going around the old city Deborah somehow gets entertained

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the city, holding it inside them
somehow says the letters of Deborah are arranged in some other way

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, the crossword's standard old city

explanation.surface: Deborah, touring an ancient city, is welcomed as a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' makes HARBOED, which goes round UR. 'entertained' sounds like amused, but means given shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour a guest or a thought is to shelter or entertain it.

clue.text: Rent leads to a bit of a fuss? A big storm!

parts.note: rent as a past participle means torn apart
ado is a bit of a fuss, a commotion

explanation.surface: A torn garment causes a minor commotion, then a full-blown storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment to a landlord, but here it is the past participle of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent rotating windstorm.

clue.text: Strong or about to break?

indicators.note: about signals turning the little word or round

parts.note: to bust something is to break it

explanation.surface: A question: is this sturdy, or on the verge of collapse?
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns OR into RO, followed by BUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust and strong both describe something sturdy and vigorous.

clue.text: Man in a hurry? That's Raymond, sir, so they say

indicators.note: so they say marks the words as spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Raymond shortens to Ray, so Ray, sir is spoken

explanation.surface: A man in a rush is identified as Raymond, addressed politely.
explanation.walkthrough: RAY SIR, said aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedster who competes to go fast is one in a hurry, a playful question-marked definition.

clue.text: Frenchman good in Paris and out of consideration with English

parts.note: bon is French for good
something set apart is excluded or left out of consideration

explanation.surface: A good Frenchman in Paris, set aside alongside an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: BONAPARTE is the family name of Napoleon, the French emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the famous French emperor, a Frenchman by example.

clue.text: Female given a sign of true love can be cutting

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
a ring, engagement or wedding, is a token of love

explanation.surface: A woman given an engagement ring might be hurtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearing means clipping, as of a sheep's fleece.

clue.text: The woman without the body part to become what she otherwise might be!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the pronoun goes round the body part

parts.note: her refers to a woman
an ear is a body part

explanation.surface: Lacking a certain organ, a woman cannot be what she would otherwise be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here means 'outside'. The definition plays on the surface: without ears she could not be a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: One with ears is a listener, which a woman lacking ears could not otherwise be.

clue.text: In respect of hypocritical talk, journalist took back words

parts.note: re means concerning or in respect of
cant is insincere pious talk
ed, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: After hypocrisy is exposed, a reporter withdraws his statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to withdraw what one said.

clue.text: Great lover seen in clubs as a star

parts.note: C is the card-playing abbreviation for clubs
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A great romantic spotted in nightclubs, a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Casanova was an 18th-century Venetian adventurer famed for his seductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova's name has become a byword for a womaniser or seducer.

clue.text: Engineers left statement after investigation

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Engineers departed after an inquiry made its statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal account of findings issued after an inquiry.

clue.text: Grim anger now getting worse, becoming very hostile

indicators.note: things getting worse are deteriorating into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bitter anger is intensifying, turning to outright aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting worse' rearranges all twelve letters of GRIM ANGER NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring up conflict and agitating for war is extremely belligerent behaviour.

clue.text: Culturally deprived state was allowed after revolution too

indicators.note: a revolution turns the word round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: let means allowed
and adds something, like too or also

explanation.surface: A nation left barren of culture after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' makes TEL. T. S. Eliot's poem 'The Waste Land' made the word a byword for cultural emptiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasteland is a barren place, figuratively a place lacking intellectual or spiritual life.

clue.text: Start of brawl? Possibly we get one to come around

definitions.text: Start of brawl? Possibly we get one to come around

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come around the single initial letter, enclosing it
possibly signals that the letters of we get one could be arranged otherwise
start of takes only the initial letter of brawl

explanation.surface: When a fight breaks out, maybe we should summon a mediator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns WE GET ONE into GOETWEEN, and 'to come around' puts B, from 'Start of brawl', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary is the person sent for to settle a dispute when a fight begins.

clue.text: Literary Frenchman unleashes anger after old dance

indicators.note: after places the word for anger behind the old dance

parts.note: the volta was a lively Renaissance dance
ire means anger

explanation.surface: A French writer loses his temper after a historic dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Voltaire was the pen name of the 18th-century French writer and philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire, author of Candide, was a famous French man of letters.

clue.text: Regard as competent and worthy of attention

parts.note: to consider is to regard
able means competent

explanation.surface: Thinking someone capable and deserving notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something considerable is significant, large enough to deserve notice.

clue.text: Broadcast from which we hear what ill-fitting carpet must be

indicators.note: we hear marks the phrase as spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a badly fitted carpet must be laid again, that is relaid

explanation.surface: A broadcast reveals what a poorly fitted carpet needs.
explanation.walkthrough: RELAID, put down again, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A transmission that is passed on, as a signal or message, has been relayed.

clue.text: Fashionable guys successfully brought aboard

indicators.note: brought here means taken into the ship, placed inside it

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the crossword's usual ship, so aboard means inside SS
well means successfully

explanation.surface: Smart men are taken onto a ship without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, a steamship, is the crossword's stock ship, so 'aboard' means inside SS; 'brought' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Swells are dandies, fashionably dressed men of high society.

clue.text: Pay attention at final moment when time is limited

indicators.note: time is limited, hemmed in, by the surrounding words

parts.note: the end is the final moment

explanation.surface: Concentrate at the last minute when time is running short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is limited' signals the insertion; 'when' is only a link. 'final moment' could suggest a deadline, but is simply END.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to heed or listen carefully.

clue.text: Something on lawn is appearing in 24 hours

indicators.note: the little word appears inside the period of time

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours

explanation.surface: Something springs up on the grass within a day.
explanation.definitionFit: A common wild flower that dots grassy lawns.

clue.text: Information at end of bulletin — number in Wales injured

indicators.note: the number sits in the shuffled letters
injured suggests the letters of Wales are damaged and rearranged

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A bulletin's final item says someone was hurt in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges WALES into LAEWS, and 'in' puts TEN between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop-press items added just before transmission or printing come at the close of a bulletin.

clue.text: Prophet seen as unconventional human

indicators.note: unconventional suggests the letters of human are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: A prophet regarded as an odd sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Long live the big town! There's animation

parts.note: viva is an exclamation meaning long live
a city is a big town

explanation.surface: A cheer for the metropolis full of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveliness and spirited energy; animation is a synonym.

clue.text: Breathe out, no longer healthy

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: An unwell person gasping for breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to expel air from the lungs.

clue.text: Fatal delay after accident at end of road

indicators.note: end of takes only the last letter of road
an accident leaves things jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deadly hold-up following a crash on the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after accident' rearranges DELAY into EADLY; 'end of road' supplies the opening D.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal and fatal both mean causing death.

clue.text: Twisted minds may display liveliness

indicators.note: twisted letters are contorted out of order

explanation.surface: Warped thinking can show surprising energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamism means energetic vigour or liveliness.
